reasons.text: Claimed tonnage in the busiest month would need 299% of the plant's connected load running non-stop (above 100% is physically impossible)
Energy charges do not match units x tariff on 100% of bills (worst bill charged 11% of expected)
Uploaded plant photos are near-duplicates of photos registered by 1 other plant(s)
52% of feedstock comes from collectors invoicing far beyond their declared capacity
Certificates claim more than the declared monthly capacity in 23% of months
100% of certificate tonnes were sold below the cost of recycling (average 0.51x the cost floor)

inspection_checklist: Obtain the DISCOM consumption statement and meter readings for the flagged months; compare connected machinery (kW) against the claimed tonnage.
Verify the electricity bills directly with the DISCOM (units, tariff, amount); the uploaded copies do not reconcile.
Compare the plant against the entities sharing its identifiers (bank, address, director, photos); consider a joint inspection.
Visit the named collectors: confirm premises, vehicles and storage; check their registration dates and sales to other buyers.
Check installed machinery and shift records against the declared capacity; request production registers for the flagged months.
Ask for the plant's cost sheet; certificates priced below the cost of recycling imply the processing cost was never incurred.
